subject: Sparkline: sudden request queueing + reserved throughput shortfall (urgent)
body:
--- Message 1 (Avery Glassman to Neha Kapoor, 2028-06-30 08:12 PDT) ---
From: Avery Glassman <avery@procure.sparkline.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Neha —

Heads up: since ~07:40 this morning we've seen a sudden jump in end-user latencies and a small wave of 5xx responses from the Redwood Dedicated endpoint (model: rwd-llama-70b-q4). Our monitoring shows request queueing building at Sparkline's reserved pool and tail latencies spiking to ~3s (previous baseline ~250ms). We've attached a short sample of logs and a CSV with KPIs.

This is impacting several high-value flows; customers are seeing retries and a ~6% drop in conversions on our payments UI. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity issue on your side (GPU saturation / reserved throughput shortfall) or something on our integration?

We need a bridge if this looks like a Redwood-side saturation — our CEO has already pinged our CRO.

Thanks,
Avery
VP Product, Sparkline Payments

--- Message 2 (Neha Kapoor to Sparkline + internal, 2028-06-30 08:28 PDT) ---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Avery Glassman <avery@procure.sparkline.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Avery —

Thanks for the data. Sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating this immediately to on-call infra and our account team. Initial readouts: your reserved pool shows a sustained concurrency bump + a small KV cache churn that increases per-token CPU. We're seeing elevated queue depth on the Dedicated instance hosts that map to your reservation.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether you kicked off any traffic ramp/feature rollout around 07:15–07:40?
- Please keep the logs coming (we have the sample).

I'm looping David (ops) for triage and Marissa so she can coordinate with your execs. We'll aim to get a remediation plan in the next 30–45 minutes and propose mitigations (burst authorization, model fallback, or temporary routing to hosted capacity).

Neha
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 (David Kim to Redwood engineering + Neha, 2028-06-30 08:52 PDT) ---
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Folks —

Triage summary (08:50):
- Observed: one reserved pool (rp-4821) serving Sparkline shows a 2.8x increase in steady QPS across the 07:30–08:30 window. Concurrently, host-level GPU utilization on two nodes reached 98–100% and the scheduler began queueing new forward requests.
- Root candidate: sudden traffic fanout from Sparkline (likely a job) combined with an inefficient request pattern (many short-lived sessions without prefix caching) — this increases kernel launch and KV cache contention on q4 quantized kernels.
- Effect: elevated p95/p99 latencies and transient 5xx from scheduler timeouts. No errors in model weights or disk I/O reported.

Short-term mitigations we can perform now:
1) Authorize burst capacity: allow Sparkline to borrow excess capacity from a cross-region burst pool (if approved by finance/leadership). This would reduce queueing within ~90s.
2) Route lower-priority endpoints to hosted (non-reserved) pool temporarily. We can maintain SLA for critical routes.
3) Apply auto-batching adjustments and bump per-request timeout on the Dedicated scheduler to reduce 5xx surface area.

I'll stand up an ops bridge if we get authorization. If leadership wants to avoid cross-customer borrowing, the fastest path is a temporary hosted fallback for non-critical routes.

-David
Director, Production Systems

--- Message 4 (Marissa Cole to Avery + internal, 2028-06-30 09:10 PDT) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Glassman <avery@procure.sparkline.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Avery —

Really sorry for the disruption. I wanted to confirm executive involvement on our side so you get a single point of contact for approvals.

Options I'll escalate to our CTO/CRO for immediate sign-off:
- Approve one-hour cross-customer burst (cost estimate attached in the internal doc); reduces queueing immediately.
- Approve temporary routing of non-critical inference calls to hosted API (we'll provide a rollout plan + IP allowlists).
- If neither is approved, we will prioritize critical endpoints only and provide staged throughput relief while we investigate longer-term fixes.

Which option gives your execs confidence? I can message our CRO now if you want us to proceed with the burst.

Marissa
Account Lead, Sparkline Strategic
Redwood Inference

--- Message 5 (Avery Glassman to Marissa/Neha, 2028-06-30 09:21 PDT) ---
From: Avery Glassman <avery@procure.sparkline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Marissa/Neha —

Please proceed with the cross-customer burst now. Our execs prefer immediate relief; we'll reconcile cost afterward. Also request that you keep the p95 tail reporting live to our SRE slack channel and flag if queue depth does not fall within 5 minutes.

We also blocked a small maintenance job last night but it shouldn't have caused this; we will double-check rollout logs and share anything we find.

Avery

--- Message 6 (Neha Kapoor to Sparkline + internal, 2028-06-30 14:03 PDT) ---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Avery Glassman <avery@procure.sparkline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and token queueing — looks tied to reserved throughput

Update and post-mortem action items:

What we did (12:10–12:20):
- Authorized a 1-hour cross-customer burst into the regional spare pool and applied an aggressive batching tuning on your Dedicated scheduler. Queue depth dropped to normal levels within ~70s. p95 latency reduced from ~2.8s -> 320ms; p99 now ~620ms.
- We routed your non-critical ingestion endpoints to Hosted as a precaution and opened instruments to watch tail latency.

Findings:
- Primary factor: a sudden traffic ramp that coincided with a low-efficiency request pattern (excess short-lived sessions without prefix reuse). This amplified kernel launch and KV cache churn on q4 pathways.
- Secondary factor: your reservation headroom metric (configured cap) was at 0 for two nodes due to a regression in autoscale headroom calculation we rolled out last week. That regression reduced measured spare capacity and prevented local transient absorb. Engineering has a patch to revert the headroom calc and will test in staging.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Infra (David) will deploy headroom fix to staging by Monday 09:00 PT and target prod rollback Wednesday (ETA 2028-07-03).
- Account (Marissa) will coordinate a credits reconciliation and discuss a request for an ongoing elevated headroom buffer with Sparkline execs (Marissa/EOD Monday).
- CS (Neha) will provide a short-runbook for Sparkline (best request patterns, prefix caching guidance, recommended timeout/backoff) by EOD Monday and schedule a joint optimization call.

Attachments: we captured the error sample and KPI snapshot you sent (attached).

We'll follow up with a formal RCA doc and timeline. Apologies for the impact — appreciate the fast approvals to get relief in.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--- End of thread ---
